6.text: Often, however, a mischievous “spirit” suddenly tugs at the skin spread

7.text: in the centre of the room with such force that things lying on it fly about

8.text: in all directions. Therefore the housemates of the shaman usually take the

9.text: precaution to remove kettles and dishes from the room. Sometimes an

10.text: invisible hand seizes the whole sleeping-room by its top, and shakes it with

11.text: wonderful strength, or even lifts it up high, letting in for a moment the

12.text: twilight from the outer tent. This, of course, is possible only with the

13.text: movable tent of the Reindeer people, where the sleeping-room is fastened

14.text: none too firmly. Other invisible hands toss about lumps of snow, spill cold

15.text: water and urine, and even throw blocks of wood, or stones, at the imminent

16.text: risk of hurting some of the listeners.

17.text: All these things happened several times in my presence. The “spirits”

18.text: would ask me, through the shamans, whether I really felt afraid; and, when

19.text: I did not give a satisfactory answer, the “spirits” would try to increase my

20.text: respect for them by such material manifestations. I must mention that the

21.text: audience is strictly forbidden to make any attempts whatever to touch the

22.text: “spirits.” These latter highly resent any intrusion of this kind, and retaliate

23.text: either on the shaman, whom they may kill on the spot, or on the trespassing

24.text: listener, who runs the risk of having his head broken, or even a knife thrust

25.text: through his ribs in the dark. I received warnings of this kind at almost

26.text: every shamanistic performance. In some cases the shaman would lay a bare

27.text: knife within his own reach as an additional warning against any infringement.

28.text: The size of the sleeping-room is so small that it is really wonderful how

29.text: a shaman can keep up the illusion, even under cover of the dark and with

30.text: the protection of his resentful “spirits.” Many times I sat so near the performer

31.text: that I could almost touch him with my outstretched hand, and the warning

32.text: against too great inquisitiveness on my part was of course quite necessary.

33.text: All these tricks strangely resemble the doings of modern spiritualists, and

34.text: without doubt they cannot be carried out without the help of human assistants.
